project_goal: Develop a dynamic graph representation learning model that effectively handles continuous-time interaction sequences with irregular time gaps and noisy historical patterns, targeting strong performance on dynamic link prediction and node classification.
method_goal: Present DyG-Mamba, a timespan-informed continuous state space model that redefines core SSM parameters to incorporate temporal irregularity and improve robustness, demonstrating how it surpasses standard SSMs on dynamic graph tasks.

obligations.author_text: Extract the first-hop interaction sequence of a node and encode it using node, edge, absolute temporal, and co-occurrence signals. Pass the aligned encoding through a continuous SSM that has been redesigned to make forgetting depend on the elapsed timespan and to selectively attend to important past inputs. Redefine the SSM step size Δt as a learnable, monotonically increasing function of the time gap, inspired by Ebbinghaus’ forgetting curve. Initialize the state transition matrix A as a diagonal matrix with negative real-part eigenvalues to guarantee stable exponential decay with increasing timespan. Redefine B and C as input-dependent matrices with spectral norm constraints, allowing the model to review important historical interactions while suppressing noise. For link prediction, use two independent DyG-Mamba encoders for source and destination nodes, pool their outputs, concatenate, and apply an MLP predictor; for node classification, use a single encoder without co-occurrence encoding.
